Index: docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
===================================================================
--- docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
+++ docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
@@ -261,7 +261,7 @@
 | `POST ledger/erasures` `{ visitorId }` | The ledger half of an erasure: writes the tombstone every reader honours at once and empties the visitor's ring. The identity erase route calls the same function after erasing the profile. `POST ledger/erasures/rewrite` runs the nightly rewrite now |
 | `GET replay/{decision_id}` | Validates recorded page dependencies, loads required prefix archives (none for a genuine pin), and compares the target including authority/exploration: `{ equal, diff[], used }`; unavailable or inconsistent dependencies fail explicitly |
 | `POST learn/report` `{ date, brand?, policies? }` and `GET learn/report?date=&brand=` | Raw attribution diagnostics from available hour aggregates, or budgeted day-ledger reads for custom policies/fallback. Explicit `policies` arrays, including empty or preset-equivalent arrays, return response-only results and never save the canonical day. Omit `policies` for ordinary canonical publication. POST bodies are limited to64KiB; raw-report budgets below return explicit413 rather than a truncated success. GET reads the stored canonical day, not a guarantee of current or settled coverage. Additive `coverage` reports source limitations; legacy `hours` and counts remain compatible. Aggregation does not establish any-size capacity or complete history. No visitor id in the result |
-| `GET learn/report/window?from=&to=&brand=` | Pools bounded stored day diagnostics over at most 92 inclusive days only where recorded slot computation bases agree. Unknown or mixed contributors withhold pooled arms with reasons/dates; found days, source counts and normalized coverage remain visible. Only genuinely missing reports enter `missing`; oversized inputs return413 and corrupt/unavailable inputs503. No experimental compatibility, inference or maturity claim |
+| `GET learn/report/window?from=&to=&brand=` | Pools bounded stored day diagnostics over at most 184 inclusive UTC days (the longest six consecutive full calendar months) only where recorded slot computation bases agree. Requested endpoints are preserved; 185 days refuse before storage I/O. Unknown or mixed contributors withhold pooled arms with reasons/dates; found days, source counts and normalized coverage remain visible. Only genuinely missing reports enter `missing`; oversized inputs return413 and corrupt/unavailable inputs503. No experimental compatibility, inference or maturity claim |
 | `POST learn/cycle[?brand=]` | Unavailable: valid authenticated requests return 503. Automatic and on-demand proposal generation/application are withdrawn pending W29 safeguards |
 | `GET learn/proposals` | Read-only historical records, explicitly unverified; retained statuses are not proof of successful application and the returned history is not guaranteed complete |
 | `POST learn/proposals/{id}/apply\|reject` | Unavailable: valid authenticated requests return 503 without proposal/configuration access or mutation |
@@ -276,7 +276,7 @@
 
 Raw reports admit at most50,000 decisions and50,000 outcomes,6 policies including learning (the existing4 presets plus1 custom fit),800 raw ledger objects,16MiB per object and combined raw UTF-8 text,1,000,000 estimated work units,16,384 projected item/slot/ancestor cells across policies, and8MiB final report JSON. Work includes ring construction/sorting, policy/outcome filtering/sorting and featured-product cross-products; listing traversal is also bounded. Consumed components are limited to256 UTF-8 bytes and generated keys to2048 bytes; invalid shapes or inherited object-property names return400. Capacity refusal returns no-store413 with `code:report_budget_exceeded`, `budget`, `limit` and `observed`, before any partial raw publication; object refusals retain `objects`/`max`. General capped loader callers retain their separate truncation contract. Native object size and actual stream bytes are checked; text-only adapters can check actual bytes only after materialization. These are application safety budgets, not proved Worker CPU/memory, supported customer traffic or scientific policy limits.
 
-Aggregate-to-day construction separately admits at most24 distinct canonical hours,16MiB combined aggregate JSON,6 policy names,1,000,000 estimated merge/admission work units,16,384 projected cells and8MiB report JSON before publication. Saved day reads admit8MiB per object; windows admit16MiB combined input and16,384 consumed/pooled rows or cells. Day/window GET responses are capped at8MiB including their response envelope. Required owner/shape failures and unavailable storage return sanitized no-store503; only an actual absent object is missing. These guards preserve accepted counts and conservative legacy coverage without rewriting stored objects. Large legacy windows can refuse even below92 days. Hour-fold/shard ingestion, configuration/tombstone loads, policy compatibility, model acceptance, full long-window measurement and native capacity remain separate work.
+Aggregate-to-day construction separately admits at most24 distinct canonical hours,16MiB combined aggregate JSON,6 policy names,1,000,000 estimated merge/admission work units,16,384 projected cells and8MiB report JSON before publication. Saved day reads admit8MiB per object; windows admit16MiB combined input and16,384 consumed/pooled rows or cells. Day/window GET responses are capped at8MiB including their response envelope. Required owner/shape failures and unavailable storage return sanitized no-store503; only an actual absent object is missing. These guards preserve accepted counts and conservative legacy coverage without rewriting stored objects. Legacy fallbacks or cardinality can refuse even below184 days; the date cap is not a native capacity guarantee. Hour-fold/shard ingestion, configuration/tombstone loads, policy compatibility, model acceptance, full long-window measurement and native capacity remain separate work.
 
 New canonical raw/hourly publications store a leading reserved `_summary` version1 in the same JSON object and the same single put as all original report fields. The summary's first line ends with comma+LF and is limited to64KiB UTF-8 including framing; the complete canonical object remains limited to8MiB. Explicit custom/empty/preset arrays remain response-only and do not acquire this storage-summary limit. Public POST/day GET report shapes remain unchanged. Window reads request the first64KiB and validate only the summary, preserving raw arm counts and normalized coverage without parsing grids. All received bytes, including chunk tails, count toward the window budget. This does not verify unread grid/tail integrity. Legacy objects use a verified complete small read or a separate bounded full read as the sole version, charging prefix plus fallback bytes; a disappeared or corrupt fallback is unavailable, not missing. Older writers can restore the coherent but slower legacy format. There is no sidecar, dual-write consistency protocol, migration or history repair. Local range/byte evidence is not deployed Worker capacity, policy compatibility or scientific/customer acceptance.
